sentences.text: Appearance:
Shri Sunil Gupta - Senior Advocate with Shri Amit Kumar   learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Santosh Singh Thakur - Govt. Advocate for the respo  ORDER

This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 51/2025 registered at Police Station- Vijayganj Mandi, District -Dewas, (M.P.) for offence punishable under Section 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC.
Applicant is in judicial custody since 16.03.2025

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this matter on complaint of wife of his brother on allegation of forging signature of his mother Sarju Bai- erstwhile Sarpanch on various bills amounting to Rs. 45, 580/-.
The FIR is registered merely on suspicion.
There is no verification of signature on bill till date.
No offence, as alleged, is made out against the applicant.
Learned counsel further submits that the applicant is aged 65 years.
Learned counsel further referring to the medical documents of District Hospital Dewas and M.Y. Hospital Indore submits that applicant had suffered paralytic attack and cardiac arrest last year.
He was admitted at District Hospital, Dewas immediately after his arrest NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9745 2 MCRC-15875-2025 wherefrom he was referred for treatment to M.Y. Hospital, Indore.
Applicant is suffering from various ailments.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion.
The prosecution is based on documentary evidence.
Therefore, there is no likelihood of tampering with evidence by ailing applicant.
Further custodial interrogation of the applicant is not needed in the matter.
The investigation is almost over.
The trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, the applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence and cites five criminal antecedents against the applicant.
In reply, learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant stand acquitted in three matters which relate to year 2004, 2010 and 2012 respectively.
Other two matters relating to year 2021 and 2022 are pending for trial.
Applicant has never been convicted.
Heard the arguments, perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in application and the case diary.
Allegedly, the applicant forged signature of his mother Sarju Bai, erstwhile Sarpanch on various bills and submitted them for payment.
The veracity of the prosecution will be determined after evidence in trial.
The report of hand-writing expert is awaited.
Since, the prosecution is based on documentary evidence, there is no likelihood of influencing the witnesses .
As informed, the applicant was aged around 65 years.
Considering these aspects, there appears to be no possibility of fleeing from justice.

In absence of any substantial criminal past and previous conviction for any major offence, considering the socio-economic status of the applicant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with evidence or influencing the witnesses by the applicant or repeating the offence.
The trial would take time to conclude.

There appears NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:9745 3 MCRC-15875-2025 to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of the ailing applicant.
However, the observations, herein-above, are recorded for present application only.

Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the case, in the light of aforesaid facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, present application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant - Vikram Singh shall be released on bail in connection with the crime as stated in para-1 of this order, upon furnishing personal bond and surety bond of amount, as may be considered appropriate by the Trial Court for compliance with conditions, as may be imposed by such Court under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C. 1973/ Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023,
to secure presence of the applicant for the trial.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial.
However, in case of breach of any of the preconditions of bail, the Trial Court may consider, on merit, cancellation of bail without any impediment of this order.
The concerned Court shall get the conditions reproduced on the personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.
If any of them is unable to write, the scribe shall certify that he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused or the surety.
C.C. as per rules.
(SANJEEV S KALGAONKAR) JUDGE sh Vikram Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162244095/
